value.rationale: The fixed graph is a canonical distance-transitive nonbipartite folded hypercube, and its skew forcing is linked to the classical minimum-skew-rank program. A complete 6490-optimum classification into nine symmetry orbits and full forcing polynomial, together with complement symmetry, connected but nonregular self-centered exchange geometry, exact 9120 Johnson-metric obstructions and failure of matroid basis exchange, give a natural structural benchmark and explicit boundary to the earlier bipartite matroid principle. No general theorem or external application is claimed.
